articles.title: Bishop seeks clean energy roadmap amid Visayas power woes
articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY — San Carlos Bishop Gerardo Alminaza on Monday described the recurring brownouts across the Visayas as a “systemic warning,” urging power sector stakeholders to reform the region’s…

blocks.text: BACOLOD CITY — San Carlos Bishop Gerardo Alminaza on Monday described the recurring brownouts across the Visayas as a “systemic warning,” urging power sector stakeholders to reform the region’s energy system instead of returning to fossil fuel dependence.
In a Facebook post, Alminaza said the continuing power interruptions were severely affecting hospitals, schools, businesses and families.

He opposed suggestions to build more coal-fired or liquefied natural gas power plants in Negros to address the power shortage, warning that such decisions could lock communities into decades of volatile fuel prices, pollution and carbon emissions.

Alminaza said the power crisis stemmed from deeper problems, including inadequate reserve margins, prolonged plant outages, transmission bottlenecks, weak inter-island grid connectivity and regulatory delays.

The prelate said the real challenge is to build renewable energy, reliability, affordability, and energy security at the same time, adding that clean energy and grid stability should not be treated as opposing choices.
To address these vulnerabilities, Alminaza proposed creating a Negros Energy Resilience and Just Transition Roadmap.
He called on the provincial government, led by Gov. Eugenio Jose Lacson, to convene key stakeholders within the next three months.

The proposed multisectoral group would include representatives from the Department of Energy, the Energy Regulatory Commission, the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines, power utilities, local governments, civil society, and consumer groups.
Alminaza said the roadmap should establish clear priorities and responsibilities to improve grid stability while ensuring long-term sustainability.

Proposed measures include transparent public assessments of plant outages and grid risks, as well as rapid resilience measures such as solar-plus-storage backup systems for critical facilities, including hospitals and water systems, within the next 12 to 24 months.

The plan also calls for expanding distributed clean energy resources, coordinating long-term transmission upgrades and establishing safeguards to protect consumers and vulnerable communities during the energy transition.
Alminaza said the current power shortages should catalyze grid modernization and clean energy expansion, not return to greater dependence on fossil fuels./coa

The LTO said Torre “voluntarily surrendered” an MMDA patrol vehicle to the agency following the issuance of the order.

articles.title: Lacson hits back at netizen who called him gay
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson disputed on Tuesday a netizen’s comment calling him gay. In a social media post where Lacson commended former House Speaker Martin Romualdez’ arrest…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson disputed on Tuesday a netizen’s comment calling him gay.
In a social media post where Lacson commended former House Speaker Martin Romualdez’ arrest in relation to the flood control mess, a netizen replied: “Bading!”
To this, Lacson responded: “You don’t know me, and I don’t know you. I’ll say it again – kung ako bading, wala ka nang makitang macho sa mundo.”
(You don’t know me, and I don’t know you. I’ll say it again – if I were gay, you wouldn’t see a macho in the world.)
Lacson has long been contradicting claims about his sexuality.

Earlier this year, the Senator said he is not gay, after Sen. Imee Marcos said she would lose if they pulled each other’s hair. Marcos later denied insinuating that Lacson is gay, saying “he has a very shallow definition of what a ‘real man’ is.”
Lacson said he has nothing against the LGBTQ community, saying “It is their choice, and I respect them for that,” noting that he “still prefers to be a real man.”
In 2013, the late Miriam Defensor-Santiago threatened to expose Lacson’s sexuality – even calling him “Pinky” Lacson.
This was also debunked by Lacson, who said: “If she’s insinuating some lunatic idea about my sexuality, let me emphasize this—I am not gay and I don’t intend to be one.” /jpv

articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Acting as one of Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense lawyers before the Senate impeachment court is lawyer Mark Vinluan. A 2014 bar passer, Vinluan earned his law degree from…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Acting as one of Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense lawyers before the Senate impeachment court is lawyer Mark Vinluan.

A 2014 bar passer, Vinluan earned his law degree from Ateneo de Manila University before joining Fortun Narvasa & Salazar Law as an associate. He stayed with the firm until 2015 before he became a partner at Vinluan Law Office.
His legal expertise mainly revolves around litigation, dispute resolution, appellate cases, corporate and commercial law, immigration, labor and intellectual property.

Since Duterte’s impeachment trial began, Vinluan has led the defense’s cross examination twice when the court tackled Article IV on grave threats—particularly when National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) regional director Jeremy Lotoc and NBI director Melvin Matibag served as witnesses.
Duterte is facing the impeachment trial amid allegations of misusing confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery and grave threats. /dp

articles.title: Marcos appoints Manny Pacquiao as anti-poverty chief
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Boxing legend Manny Pacquiao has returned to public service after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. appointed him as the lead convenor of the National Anti-Poverty Commission…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Boxing legend Manny Pacquiao has returned to public service after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. appointed him as the lead convenor of the National Anti-Poverty Commission (NAPC) with a rank of Cabinet secretary.

Pacquiao, 47, is scheduled to take his oath before Marcos at Malacañang on Tuesday, according to the Presidential Communications Office (PCO). First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos and Cabinet Secretary Benhur Abalos are expected to attend the ceremony.
He replaced Lope Santos III, who had served as NAPC lead convenor since 2023.

Established through Republic Act No. 8425, the NAPC shall coordinate poverty reduction programs by national and local governments, and ensure that marginalized sectors participate in government decision-making processes.
It is chaired by Marcos, while Pacquiao, as lead convenor, shall serve as head of the NAPC Secretariat.

Pacquiao’s appointment came after Marcos issued Executive Order No. 123, transferring the oversight and control of the NAPC and the Presidential Commission for the Urban Poor (PCUP) from the Department of Social Welfare (DSWD) to the Office of the President (OP).
The post of Pacquiao is different from that of Secretary Larry Gadon, who currently serves as Marcos’ presidential adviser for poverty alleviation.

Pacquiao is widely regarded as one of the greatest professional boxers of all time, becoming the only eight-division world champion in boxing history. He has won twelve major world titles overall and was inducted to the International Boxing Hall of Fame in 2025.
He served as a member of Congress for 12 consecutive years: as district representative of Sarangani from 2010 to 2016, and then senator from 2016 to 2022.
Pacquiao ran for president in the 2022 general elections and lost to Marcos.
In that same month, he announced his intention to retire from professional boxing.
Three years later, Pacquiao became a senatorial candidate for the 2025 midterm elections under the banner of President Marcos’ Alyansa para sa Bagong Pilipinas.
He eventually lost his bid for the Senate, placing 18th out of the 12 seats up for election, garnering 10,397,133 votes.
In July 2025, Pacquiao announced his intention to retire from politics and his return to boxing. /jpv

articles.title: Flights to Jakarta resume after volcanic ash forced 2-day closure of several Indonesian airports
articles.summary: Flights to and from Indonesia's capital of Jakarta resumed early Tuesday after ash from a volcanic eruption forced a two-day closure that halted nearly 3,000 flights.

image.caption: A stranded passenger waits as Soekarno-Hatta International Airport closed its operations due to the eruption Sunday of Mount Anak Krakatau volcano. Flights to and from Jakarta resumed Tuesday. (Ajeng Dinar Ulfiana/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
Flights to and from Indonesia's capital of Jakarta resumed early Tuesday after ash from a volcanic eruption forced a two-day closure that halted nearly 3,000 flights.
Nearly 3,000 flights were affected following the eruption of Anak Krakatau

Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and Halim Perdanakusuma Airport serving Jakarta, Husein Sastranegara Airport in West Java's Bandung city and two smaller airports in Banten province reopened just after midnight, Indonesia's Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said.

Three other airports remained closed until 10 a.m. local time, including Radin Inten II Airport in Lampung on the southern tip of Sumatra island, despite improving conditions at some facilities. Atung Bungsu Airport in Pagar Alam in South Sumatra province had resumed normal operations Monday morning.

"We are taking a conservative approach because wind direction is highly dynamic," Purwagandhi said in a statement. "We want to ensure that volcanic ash has moved away from airports around Anak Krakatau."

Although tests at several airports showed no traces of volcanic ash, the extended closures would allow time for inspecting and cleaning surfaces and equipment like runways, taxiways and aircraft that may have been exposed to volcanic ash, Purwagandhi said.
The continuous eruption of Anak Krakatau with lava fountains and loud booms ended Sunday but the volcanic island remained active Tuesday morning.
The airport closures Sunday and Monday disrupted nearly 2,961 flights, including 622 international services, and affected about 341,000 passengers.

articles.title: LIST: Big names, others arrested in flood control scandal
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The government’s investigation into alleged corruption in flood control and other infrastructure projects has led to the arrest and detention of several personalities, with the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The government’s investigation into alleged corruption in flood control and other infrastructure projects has led to the arrest and detention of several personalities, with the cases now reaching some of the country’s most prominent political figures.

The flood control scandal came to national prominence in August 2025 after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. exposed an allegedly nonexistent P55-million river wall project in Bulacan, prompting a government review of nearly 10,000 flood control projects, a Senate probe, and the creation of the Independent Commission for Infrastructure (ICI) to investigate alleged anomalies and kickbacks.

Marcos made the flood control issue a centerpiece of his 2025 State of the Nation Address (Sona), calling out officials and contractors allegedly involved in corruption, saying “Mahiya naman kayo!” (You should be ashamed of yourselves)

In the months that followed, cases were filed and arrests were made involving contractors, DPWH officials, and lawmakers. However, critics still questioned when the so-called “big fish” will be caught.

In his 2026 Sona, Marcos said the investigation would proceed without favor and stressed this even as the cases reached his first cousin, former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, saying, “Hindi ako Pangulo ng aking pamilya… Ako ay Pangulo ng Pilipinas.”
(I am not the President of my family… I am the President of the Philippines.)
But who have been arrested?
High-profile personalities

items: Martin Romualdez – former House Speaker and incumbent Leyte 1st District representative; arrested on Sept. 7, 2026 after the Sandiganbayan ordered his detention over a P7.44-billion plunder case involving alleged kickbacks from flood control, infrastructure and other government projects.
Sen. Jinggoy Estrada – arrested after surrendering to the PNP-CIDG on June 1, 2026 over a nonbailable plunder case linked to alleged kickbacks from flood control projects.

Former Sen. Bong Revilla – arrested alongside several DPWH officials over a P92.8-million flood control project in Pandi, Bulacan. Revilla later posted bail in the graft case, while the malversation case remained nonbailable. The Sandiganbayan subsequently granted him temporary release.

Manuel “Manny” Bonoan – former DPWH secretary; surrendered to authorities after being ordered arrested over a plunder case linked to the flood control scandal. He was later removed as an accused in the case and released by the Sandiganbayan.

blocks.text: Contractors

items: Pacifico “Curlee” Discaya – contractor; arrested at the Senate on June 8, 2026 after a warrant was issued over a malversation case involving an alleged P53.9-million anomalous flood control project in Calumpit, Bulacan.
Cezarah “Sarah” Discaya – contractor; detained in connection with the alleged P96.5-million “ghost” flood control project in Jose Abad Santos, Davao Occidental.
Ma. Roma Angeline Rimando – managing officer of St. Timothy Construction Corp.; surrendered to Pasig City police and was subsequently placed in custody in connection with the Davao Occidental case.

blocks.text: Estrada/Bonoan plunder case

items: Denryl Caesar Cortuna – former DPWH NCR assistant district engineer; arrested and detained in connection with the plunder case involving Estrada and Bonoan.
Manny Bulusan – former DPWH district engineer; arrested and detained in the same case.
Arturo Gonzales Jr. – former DPWH district engineer; arrested and detained in the same case.

blocks.text: The Sandiganbayan also ordered the arrest of Ernesto Cosay Galang and Lorenzo Alcoriza Pagtalunan, who remained at large.
Oriental Mindoro – P289.4-million case
Moreover, nine DPWH officials from the Mimaropa region were likewise placed under government custody over an alleged anomalous P289.4-million road dike project in Oriental Mindoro:

articles.title: Praying for rain as fires, haze plague Indonesian Borneo
articles.summary: PONTIANAK, Indonesia — Wildfires ravaging the Indonesian part of Borneo island are choking communities as far away as Malaysia with putrid haze, testing the resources and resolve of those…

blocks.text: PONTIANAK, Indonesia — Wildfires ravaging the Indonesian part of Borneo island are choking communities as far away as Malaysia with putrid haze, testing the resources and resolve of those having to endure them.

Blamed partly on one of the worst episodes of the drought-inducing El Nino weather phenomenon in decades, the disaster threatens millions of people’s access to necessities such as clean water and air — even education.
Here is the situation as seen from the perspective of three community leaders in Indonesia’s West Kalimantan province, one of the worst-affected regions:
The teacher
Syarifah Hatifah, the 57-year-old vice principal of a junior high school in provincial capital Pontianak, fears some of her nearly 600 pupils may be falling behind.
They are in the third week of the second school closure this fire season. It’s the longest closure Syarifah can remember in her 30-year career.
Hundreds of schools have been closed indefinitely in West Kalimantan due to air pollution, with about 200,000 pupils learning from home, according to the provincial education ministry.
The kids are being kept home for their health, Syarifah told AFP in a classroom empty but for two teachers presenting classes online, both with dozens of pupils scattered across their screens.
“The hope is that at home, in terms of health, they can be protected… because they are inside the house. They don’t have to go through roads full of dust and smoke,” she said.
But Syarifah said not every child has stable internet or access to a computer, making live sessions difficult for some.
“Sometimes… there is a power outage at their home, or they forget to charge their phones”, and some students live in faraway areas with patchy connectivity, she said.
The school’s teachers have been showing up every day as usual, giving lessons online in classrooms with no air purifiers. They work maskless so students can understand them clearly.
Syarifah said the school would offer extra lessons for free once in-person learning resumes.
“We hope that this haze will pass quickly. Usually after the rain falls, the haze will disappear,” she said.
West Kalimantan’s wetter season usually starts around October or November.
The health official
Iwansyah, head of the Kubu Raya regency’s health agency, is responsible for the welfare of some 700,000 people spread over 123 villages, served by one general hospital and 21 clinics.
His staff focus on efforts to prevent illness caused by “the unhealthy air people inhale every day”.
So far in September, more than 1,400 people in the regency have been treated or hospitalised for acute respiratory infections, said Iwansyah, who like many Indonesians has one name.

blocks.caption: An aerial view shows the Ampera Bridge over the Musi river shrouded in haze caused by forest fires in Palembang, South Sumatra on September 3, 2026. Agence France-Presse

blocks.text: In August, the number was 6,396.
“We distribute masks to the public every day, about one thousand masks per day. Of course our stock is starting to run low,” the official told AFP.
Iwansyah said the agency had requested additional masks from the provincial government, and was encouraging people to buy their own.
The agency also monitors cases of diarrhoea brought on by reduced access to clean water due to the drought, with 225 cases so far this month.

With Indonesia’s BMKG weather agency warning of little respite in the weeks ahead, “we will have to work even harder on mitigation and preparing for a potentially very severe situation”, said Iwansyah.
This includes stocking up on medicines and equipment at clinics and intensifying surveys of water and air quality.
“Hopefully there will be rain between now and November,” Iwansyah said.
The hamlet head
For Yonas, deputy head of the Lintang Batang hamlet outside Pontianak, the priority is firefighting equipment.

“The residents here even pooled money to buy a (water pump) machine and hoses, and other equipment,” he told AFP on Sunday night while battling a peatland fire that had been raging for four days, emitting acrid smoke.
“We’re still short of hoses, which makes it hard for us to extinguish this fire.”

Volunteer firefighters were using “whatever we have. Sometimes we use buckets, and even those aren’t enough”, said Yonas, adding that the teams were also in need of food and protective gear, including masks.
He said the smoke posed a danger especially for children, pregnant women, the elderly and people with asthma.
Scientific observations show the haze contains levels of toxic small particle pollution far exceeding the World Health Organization’s recommended safe limit.
“It’s very hazardous to the health of us who live in this village,” said Yonas. /dl

articles.title: Prosecutors ask ICC to examine documents linking ex-Pres Duterte to DDS
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecutors have asked Trial Chamber III to examine documents submitted by a witness that may link former President Rodrigo Duterte to the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecutors have asked Trial Chamber III to examine documents submitted by a witness that may link former President Rodrigo Duterte to the Davao Death Squad or DDS.

According to the document made public Monday, Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang filed a request on August 31 seeking permission for the witness, identified as “P-1100,” to submit a statement instead of testifying in person.

The prosecution cited Rule 68 of the ICC Rules of Procedure and Evidence, which allows parties to invoke prior recorded testimony before a witness’s scheduled testimony. However, such submissions remain subject to cross-examination and questioning by the Trial Chamber.
“The Prior Recorded Testimony of P-1100… is particularly relevant to the policy to ‘neutralise’ through violent crimes, including murder, alleged criminals in the Philippines,” Niang wrote.
He continued: “It also provides evidence of the Davao Death Squad’s modus operandi as well as [Duterte’s] criminal responsibility, including in relation to his knowledge and intent.”
Primarily, the prosecution reasoned that the request is to expedite Duterte’s proceedings, “having the health of [Duterte] in mind.”
Niang also wrote that, should the request be granted, the length of the witness’ direct examination would be reduced from seven hours to two hours.

Duterte is facing two counts of murder as crimes against humanity, and one count of attempted murder and murder as a crime against humanity for his supposed role in the drug war as president of the Philippines and as Davao City mayor.
His trial is scheduled to commence on November 30, 2026. /jpv

articles.title: Romualdez seeks hospital custody until medically cleared
articles.summary: The former speaker cited Manuel Bonoan who was allowed to remain hospitalized while in custody.

blocks.text: September 8, 2026 | 9:54am

Rep. Martin Romualdez (Leyte) lies in a hospital bed at Cardinal Santos Medical Center as police place him under custody on Sept. 7, 2026, following the Sandiganbayan's issuance of a warrant in a P7.44-billion plunder case.
Philstar.com / Contributed photo

MANILA, Philippines — Rep. Martin Romualdez (Leyte) asked the Sandiganbayan to allow him to remain under custody at Cardinal Santos Medical Center until doctors clear him for transfer to a detention facility.

In a manifestation and urgent motion late Monday, September 7, Romualdez's lawyers said his request was not an attempt to avoid arrest or custody, but an accommodation for what they described as documented medical needs requiring continued inpatient care.
"Accused Romualdez has a documented cardiac history and has remained under continuing care for that condition," the manifestation read.

Romualdez proposed a court-supervised arrangement that would include round-the-clock guards, visitor restrictions and a visitor log, periodic medical certificates, independent verification of his condition and a prohibition on leaving or transferring from the hospital without court approval except for medical emergencies.

"Accused seeks no exemption from arrest, custody, booking, security restrictions, court appearances, or eventual transfer to the detention facility designated by the Honorable Court," the motion said.
His lawyers asked that he remain at Cardinal Santos "for so long as inpatient confinement remains medically necessary" and until he is medically cleared for transfer.

The filing cited Romualdez's history of cardiovascular disease and several other conditions, as well as an angioplasty he underwent in October 2024. It also lists other conditions including hypertension, coronaru artery disease, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and hypothyroidism.

It also cited a June Sandiganbayan ruling that allowed former Public Works secretary Manuel Bonoan to remain under hospital arrest despite a no-bail recommendation, subject to government medical evaluation, security and regular reports to the court. Bonoan has since been released from detention on the promise of his testimony as state witness to how public flood-control funds have been siphoned through private contractors and substandard or nonexistent projects.
Romualdez was arrested Monday night at Cardinal Santos after the Sandiganbayan issued a warrant over a P7.44-billion plunder case filed by the Ombudsman.

Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said police would check Romualdez's condition daily until he was well enough to be presented to court. Armed police were stationed outside his room while he remained under custody.
The Sandiganbayan has said it would make its own assessment of whether Romualdez's medical condition affects his transfer to a regular detention facility. — with reports from Ian Laqui

articles.title: UK government expected to announce restrictions on trade with West Bank settlements
articles.summary: Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is expected to outline proposals targeting goods from Israeli-occupied areas on Tuesday.
articles.byline: Paul Adams, Nicholas Watt, Henry Moore

blocks.text: The UK government is to set out new restrictions on buying goods made in Jewish settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, the BBC understands.
Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is expected to outline the measures in the Commons on Tuesday, which could include restrictions on trade in agricultural products from settlements.
Last week, Miliband said he would unveil a "comprehensive reset" of the British government's policy on Israel.
The Israeli government has previously warned it would retaliate if any new measures were introduced.
Settlements are illegal under international law, and recent months have seen a rise in violence towards Palestinians in the West Bank by settlers.
One minister told the BBC: "The statement will be a complete reset of the nature of our Israel-Palestine relationship. It will all feel very different.
"It is not just about sanctions. We hope that this will finally achieve what those of us who have been working towards for two years over the Middle East have been working on."
BBC News has not seen the full details of the measures.
But Labour MPs who have been briefed on the plans believe the sanctions will target trade with illegal settlements. They believe that means the sanctions would cover both goods and services.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham confirmed to Labour MPs at their weekly parliamentary meeting on Monday night that Miliband would be making the statement, according to a number of MPs present.
The prime minister is also said to have told the meeting that he had briefed international leaders about plans in phone calls on Monday afternoon.
Burnham spoke to US President Donald Trump over the phone on Monday, during which the prime minister stressed the importance of a two-state solution in the Middle East.
An official account of the call released by No 10 did not specify that Burnham had briefed Trump on the sanctions, while the US - which is likely to strongly oppose the proposals - has not commented.

Speaking in July, Stephen Doughty - who was then Europe minister but has since been appointed Middle East minister - told the business select committee that existing powers to impose restrictions on settlements did not go far enough.

He said: "At the moment, we can sanction where there is evidence of it being linked to settler violence, but not, for example, in relation to a contractor working on the settlements. We need to expand our sanctions powers."

While ministers are said to recognise that banning a relatively small quantity of mostly agricultural products is a largely symbolic gesture, the government is expected to frame this announcement as a major reset in Britain's wider policy on Israel.

The expected announcement by the UK government comes after Israel opened up tenders for the construction of some 1,200 settlement homes in the so-called E1 area - a strategically important area east of Jerusalem. The plans have drawn widespread international condemnation.
Israel has held off on plans to build in the area for decades under global pressure.

Speaking in his first address to Parliament as foreign secretary last week, Miliband said those plans were "illegal under international law", and called them "the crossing of a red line, as it cuts through the heart of the West Bank and risks making a Palestinian state unviable".
Prime Minister Andy Burnham also warned that Israel's announcement about the E1 area could "imperil or end" the two-state solution in the Middle East.

Tuesday's expected intervention will come almost a year after Sir Keir Starmer's government recognised a state of Palestine, and said the UK had a moral responsibility to support a peaceful future for Israelis and Palestinians.
The government believes the prospect of a two-state solution is being jeopardised by the rapid expansion of settlements.
The proposal for an independent Palestinian state in the West Bank and Gaza, with East Jerusalem as its capital, to exist alongside Israel has received international backing over several decades.
Israel rejects a two-state solution. The Palestinian Authority backs a two-state solution but Hamas does not because it is opposed to the existence of Israel.

Israel has built about 160 settlements housing 700,000 Jews since it occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem - land Palestinians want, along with Gaza, for a hoped-for future state - during the 1967 Middle East war. An estimated 3.3 million Palestinians live alongside them.

There has been a surge in attacks by settlers on Palestinians and their property in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, which was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023.

articles.title: Trial over alleged murders of Australian surfer brothers starts in Mexico
articles.summary: The bodies of Jake and Callum Robinson and their US friend were found with gunshot wounds to their heads.

blocks.text: Three men have gone on trial in Mexico for the alleged murders of two Australian brothers and their American friend in 2024.

The bodies of Callum Robinson, his younger brother Jake, and their friend Carter Rhoad from California - all in their early 30s - were found at the bottom of a well with gunshot wounds to their heads, days after they went missing during a surf trip in Baja California.
Prosecutors are seeking jail sentences of more than 200 years for the defendants, who also face charges of violent robbery and auto theft.
The parents of the brothers were in court on Tuesday in the coastal town of Ensenada, telling the media that it was "incredibly important and overwhelmingly difficult".

"We want the men accused of murdering our sons to see, in person, the human consequences of what happened," Martin and Debra Robinson said in a statement, according to Australia's national broadcaster, the ABC.
"Callum and Jake were not simply victims in a case file - they were our sons, deeply loved by their family and friends, with lives, dreams and futures that were brutally taken away."

On the opening day, the accused - Jesús "El Kekas" Gerardo, Irineo Francisco and Ángel Jesús - were moved to a smaller courtroom amid accusations that some witnesses had been intimidated by people associated with the defendants.
Dozens of witnesses are expected to give evidence during the four-week, judge-only trial.
The 2024 alleged killings of the Robinson brothers and their US friend shocked Australians as well as many residents of the normally peaceful town of Ensenada.
Despite high levels of cartel violence in the northern Mexican border states, tourists are rarely targeted for such violent attacks in Baja California's surf towns.

The ex-girlfriend of one of the accused, Ari Gisell, became the first person to be convicted over the tourists' killings last year and was sentenced to 20 years in prison for her role in their murders.
Mexican prosecutors are pursuing jail sentences of more than 200 years for each of the defendants, as well as an additional 168-year sentence for the alleged ringleader.
Prosecutors say the victims were killed due to a bungled robbery, while the defence argued there was not enough evidence to prove that theory.
Callum Robinson was a member of Australia's national lacrosse team and lived in San Diego where he was a professional lacrosse player.
His younger brother Jake had travelled from Australia for the surf trip and was due to start a job as a doctor when he returned while their friend Rhoad was killed a few months before his wedding.

blocks.text: Ukraine's chief prosecutor Ruslan Kravchenko has resigned over corruption allegations related to illegal call centres in the country.
It follows a search of his offices over the weekend by Ukrainian anti-corruption investigators, who said they had identified a money-laundering scheme led by an official in Kravchenko's office.

In his resignation letter, Kravchenko said he did not want his position to be used as a "tool for political confrontation", and referenced an earlier post in which he rejected the claims as "unsubstantiated".
Corruption scandals have plagued Kyiv throughout the war against Russia, with accusations levelled at several members of President Volodymyr Zelensky's inner circle.

According to Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau (Nabu) and Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (Sap), the network in Kravchenko's office received money to protect call centres that carried out phone scams and "laundered millions in assets".
The money was then used to buy property, jewellery, and other valuables, according to Nabu.
Kravchenko released a statement on Sunday evening dismissing the allegations as "completely unsubstantiated", and denied any wrongdoing.
He tendered his resignation a day later, thanking Zelensky and the Ukrainian parliament for their "trust". The Ukrainian president is yet to comment publicly on the resignation.
Despite the creation of two Ukrainian anti-corruption bodies, Nabu and Sap, over a decade ago, corruption continues to be a significant problem in the country.
In 2025, nationwide protests broke out after Zelensky tried to implement reforms that would curb the independence of Nabu and Sap.
Kyiv's European partners expressed alarm at the announcement, with ambassadors from the G7 group of nations warning it could endanger Ukraine's integration into the European Union.
Ukraine is an EU candidate country, a status it was granted on condition it mounted a credible fight against corruption.
Zelensky reinstated the freedom of the two anti-corruption bodies as a result of the backlash, but questions have persisted over his commitment to anti-corruption reform.
Last month, Nabu said it had uncovered a scheme to misappropriate more than $3m (£2.2m) in Ukrainian currency to pay bail for a former energy minister accused of money laundering.
A senior official in Zelensky's office alleged to be involved was sacked.

articles.title: New prize named for late author Andrew Pyper will recognize horror and thriller writers
articles.summary: Heidi Pyper says she's frustrated that horror and thriller writers like her late husband, Andrew Pyper, don't get the recognition they deserve, noting that he wasn't considered for Canada's top…

image.caption: Heidi Pyper, left, is shown with her late husband, author Andrew Pyper. She says the Andrew Pyper Prize for Genre Fiction honours his legacy and will encourage other horror and thriller authors. (Submitted by Heidi Pyper)

blocks.text: The Current·New

Heidi Pyper says she's frustrated that horror and thriller writers like her late husband, Andrew Pyper, don't get the recognition they deserve, noting that he wasn't considered for Canada's top literary prizes because of the genre of his books. She hopes a new prize will help honour his legacy and encourage other writers.
Announcement of $20,000 award coincides with release of Pyper's final novel
LISTEN | New $20,000 literary prize created to honour Andrew Pyper's legacy:
The Current8:12A new writing prize honouring Andrew Pyper
Heidi Pyper says her late husband, Andrew, wasn't just a bestselling author. He was also generous, curious and truly cared about people.
Affectionately known as "Canada's Stephen King," Andrew died in January 2025 of complications from cancer at the age of 56.

He was a prolific and acclaimed writer of horror, thrillers and other types of speculative fiction, including The Killing Circle and The Demonologist, and Pyper said her husband wrote characters who had great depth.
But she said she's frustrated that writers like Andrew don't get the recognition they deserve, noting there aren't many genre-specific awards available for horror or thriller writing.
That's why Andrew's friend and fellow author, Craig Davidson, helped create the Andrew Pyper Prize for Genre Fiction.

items: Acclaimed thriller writer Andrew Pyper dead at age 56

blocks.text: The $20,000 prize will be administered through the Writers’ Trust of Canada. To be eligible to win, writers must have published at least three books in the horror, thriller or speculative fiction genre. Thanks to a massive campaign, enough money has been raised to support the prize for seven years.
The announcement for the award coincides with the release of Andrew's final novel, Driven.
As a reader and writer of horror, he believed that the genre could expand people’s understanding of the human condition.
Pyper said she hopes the prize will help support and encourage authors like Andrew. She spoke to Matt Galloway, host of The Current, about the prize and legacy she wants it to leave.
When you listen to Andrew talk about horror and the human condition, what's going through your mind?

It brings such a smile to my face hearing Andrew talk about horror, thriller and genre writing in a way that's deep and meaningful because he brought a lot of depth to his writing. Particularly with the characters that he put under great duress. I remember my dad reading The Wildfire Season and saying, "Why does he keep putting these people I care about in such jeopardy?" And I was like, "That's the trick."
When he died, there was this huge outpouring of sadness from this country and beyond. There are people who perhaps only know him from his books. Tell us a little bit more about Andrew.

It's hard to talk about Andrew without sounding hyperbolic, but he really was a lovely man. He was smart, funny and talented. I would be remiss if I didn't mention how good-looking he was. People really loved him.

items: Remembering celebrated Canadian thriller author Andrew Pyper

blocks.text: Many writers told stories of him and his generosity towards them, encouraging them to write, agreeing to come into classrooms to talk to students. The other thing that people kept saying was how he made them feel, he made them feel important. I think that stems from his curiosity. So when you were talking to Andrew, he didn't want to talk about himself, he wanted to hear about you and what was going on in your life.
This idea for this writing prize, in many ways, speaks to the generosity that he had. I'm sure he’d love this idea.
I think he'd be quite chuffed.
Tell me more about this prize and how the idea for this sparked.

Andrew played poker with a group of guys – writers, bookish-professor types – and he was no gambler, but he was dedicated to this group. About six months after Andrew died, Craig Davidson came to me and floated the idea, asked me what I thought and if it was OK if they tried to pursue this. Of course, I thought it was a wonderful idea.

Then he made the mistake of asking if I wanted to help. I'm sure he regretted that because I'd show up with my to-do list and a work-back schedule. But it came out of love and friendship amongst these men who played cards together.
But also from the fact that Andrew, despite the fact that he was a bestseller and wrote great books, didn't get the nod from some of those "literary prizes in Canada."
Yes, I think that was a frustration for him that he was disqualified before even being considered.

It wasn't like he was nominated and didn't win. It feels like there's a gap. Genre props up the publishing industry, people gobble it up. Movies and television are made from our writing, and it feels like a missing piece in the awards landscape. They recognized that, and the Pyper Prize began in that spirit.
It'll be $20,000.
It's a good chunk of change.

I think that's the distinction. There are awards for thriller writers and horror writers that exist. There's the [Bram Stoker Award], the Shirley Jackson [Award], I think there's the International Thriller Writers Awards but none of them come with a prize purse. So this really is a one-of-a-kind prize, not just in Canada, but we have yet to find one that is the equivalent.
The prize arrives at the same time as his new book comes out.

Yes. So Andrew left us with a few final words. Driven is the third and final book under his pseudonym Mason Coile. So the confluence of these two things happening at the same time is really meaningful.
How are you doing in all of this?

It's a lot, I'm not going to lie. I say it's very weird to have someone who has left us be so top of mind and such an ongoing concern, I kind of live with him in my head. I've elected to keep his social media active. His publisher offered to do it, but I just felt like I wanted to keep control of that.
In some ways, the book and the prize mean that the legacy lives on, there's a voice that’s still there.

I just reread Driven a couple of weeks ago. I read it when he finished it, but he was so sick when he was writing, it was right at the end of his life. He had said to me, "Should I write another book?" And I said, "Yeah, what else are you going to do? It's the thing that's going to get you up in the morning.” I started to read it then, but it was too dark. I said, “Our life is too scary for me to read this.” So I just read it again and you can really hear his voice. The sound of it is very clear in my mind.
Interview produced by Enza Uda

articles.title: Nepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster
articles.summary:
Foreign minister Shisir Khanal tells the Guardian the world’s biggest economies need to help Nepal, which contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions

Nepal is demanding…

blocks.text: Nepal is demanding $20m in climate compensation for the recent devastating floods, as a senior minister called on the world’s most polluting countries to “wake up” and accept shared responsibility for a disaster that led to the death or disappearance of more than 6,000 people.

Scientists believe the climate crisis had a role to play in the floods, which were triggered when a melting glacier partially collapsed and set off a deadly landslide and flash flooding through Chinese-controlled Tibet and Nepal in late August. So far, more than 1,300 are confirmed dead and more than 5,500 still missing, with hopes of their survival diminished after 12 days of rescue operations.

Speaking to the Guardian, Nepal’s foreign minister, Shisir Khanal, was forthright in his call for climate justice and said it was imperative the world’s biggest economies stepped up to help Nepal recover and rebuild after the catastrophic floods.

Nepal contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions, while its neighbours India and China are among the world’s biggest emitters. The mountains of the Himalayas – which span across India, China, Nepal and Bhutan – have been warming at a rate nearly 50% faster than the global average.
In 2023, the UN said Nepal’s mountains had lost close to a third of their ice in just over 30 years due to global heating.

Khanal emphasised that the recent disaster was far more extreme than any flooding regularly seen during the monsoon season, and said the magnitude of damage was on par with the 2015 earthquake that left much of the country in ruins.

blocks.caption: An excavator repairs a damaged road in Nepal near the Trishuli River on Monday. Photograph: Anushree Fadnavis/Reuters

blocks.text: “This felt like a tsunami that was coming from the Himalayas,” he said. “We experienced waves as high as 60, 70 feet, which were mixed with debris, mud, stones, rocks, and came at the speed of almost 180km per hour. Towns, villages and highways were completely wiped out and there are some areas still disconnected.”

Khanal confirmed that Nepal’s ministry of finance and ministry of environment had written a joint letter to the UN’s fund for responding to loss and damage – which was set up in 2022 in line with the Paris climate agreement – to request $20m in climate-related damages.

“We have contributed so little to climate change,” he said. “It is imperative for those in the global community who benefit from larger, much more polluting economies, and whose historical contribution to greenhouse gases is much bigger than ours, to accept a shared responsibility. This affects all of humanity.”
For Nepal, the disaster was particularly worrying because it was “one of the strongest warning signals that we’ve experienced of what’s to come”, he said.

“The global community should not see this as one-off disaster; it should be viewed in the context of the changing climate in the Himalayas,” he said. “We know it is going to be a recurring scenario that more and more communities, not just in Nepal but around the world, will have to face.”

Khanal acknowledged that the compensation amount Nepal has requested from the UN was “obviously not nearly enough to cover the damage that we have sustained”. According to some estimates, the total damage caused by the floods will be upwards of $5bn, though Khanal said it could be even higher.

Upwards of 20,000 homes will probably have to be rebuilt, as well as the main highway. Villages built in vulnerable areas along the river, some of which washed away entirely, may have to be relocated to higher, safer ground.

While Khanal initially singled out India and China as countries that should step in to help – while avoiding mention of the US, which is the world’s biggest polluter – he rowed back on those comments, saying: “It is not just about shifting the blame to one or the other country, it’s about us all working together.”

blocks.caption: Damaged buildings on the banks of the Trishuli River. Photograph: Anushree Fadnavis/Reuters

blocks.text: He emphasised that the compensation demand was also meant to act as a “wake-up call for the global community to establish a more robust mechanism to help vulnerable and small economies like Nepal”.

The UN has admitted the loss and damage fund is already facing a “significant financing gap”. The fund has already received requests totalling $2.8bn from about 119 countries, but so far only around $400m has been given by the international community. The US has given just $17m, after Donald Trump withdrew from the Paris agreement.
Khanal acknowledged there were “political challenges” in getting Nepal the climate compensation it was demanding.
“Yes there always will be people who may not agree to our perspective or deny there is climate change, but there are also people who deny that the Earth is round,” he said bluntly.
He emphasised the importance of funds being made available not just for immediate disaster response but also for preparedness and mitigation for climate-related risk.

Khanal rebuffed allegations that China had failed to give an adequate warning or share data with Nepal about the impending floods. He said he was in discussion with China about enhancing coordination and data sharing for the Himalayan region.
“With the benefit of hindsight, we can now see that this glacier was fragile and had been receding in the past six months,” he said.

“But before the floods hit, there was no knowledge on our part, or on the part of Chinese scientists, that this particular collapse was imminent. I do not believe any of us had any idea of the threat until it happened.”

blocks.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.
On this page, we bring you the latest updates, analyses, videos, and photos as the trial of the Vice President unfolds.

articles.title: Habagat rains to persist over Luzon, Visayas
articles.summary: Several areas in Luzon and Visayas may experience rains on Tuesday, September 8, as the southwest monsoon or habagat continues to affect the country, PAGASA said.

blocks.text: September 8, 2026 | 8:32am
Pedestrians struggle with their umbrellas against strong winds during a sudden heavy downpour in Quezon City on Aug. 28, 2026.
The Philippine STAR / Miguel de Guzman
MANILA, Philippines — Several areas in Luzon and Visayas may experience rains on Tuesday, September 8, as the southwest monsoon or habagat continues to affect the country, PAGASA said.
In its 5 a.m. weather forcecast, the state weather bureau said that no tropical cyclone is being monitored inside or near the Philippine area of responsibility.
Weather specialist Veronica Torres, however, said the possibility of a low-pressure area forming remains.
Zambales and Bataan will bear the brunt of the habagat, with 100 to 200 millimeters of rainfall expected in the next 24 hours.
“Asahan natin 'yung monsoon rains sa Zambales at Bataan. Kapag monsoon rains, ito 'yung halos tuloy-tuloy na moderate to heavy rains,” Torres said.
(We can expect monsoon rains over Zambales and Bataan. These monsoon rains are almost continuous, ranging from moderate to heavy.)
The rainfall forecast may trigger flooding, particularly in urbanized, low-lying and riverside areas, while landslides may occur in areas highly susceptible to the hazard.
Meanwhile, Pangasinan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Cavite, Batangas and Occidental Mindoro may experience occasional rains, with rainfall amounts reaching 50 to 100 mm.
Flash floods and landslides are also possible in these areas due to moderate to heavy rains.
Metro Manila and the rest of Luzon will have cloudy skies with scattered rain showers and thunderstorms. PAGASA said flash floods and landslides may occur due to moderate to at times heavy rains.
Torres said the habagat may affect a wider portion of Luzon in the coming days before its influence gradually weakens.

Western Visayas will have cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms due to the habagat. The rest of the region will experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms.
Mindanao, meanwhile, will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms due to localized thunderstorms.
PAGASA warned of possible flash floods and landslides in areas affected by severe thunderstorms.
Winds over Luzon and Visayas will be light to moderate and generally move from the southwest to west, while coastal waters will remain light to moderate.
Mindanao will have light to moderate winds moving from the south to southwest, with slight to moderate coastal waters.
No gale warning is currently in effect over any seaboard in the country, PAGASA said.

articles.title: Rescued endangered hawk-eagle eaglet turned over to DENR in Zamboanga
articles.summary: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – A juvenile South Philippine Hawk-Eagle (Nisaetus pinskeri), an endangered raptor endemic to the country, was rescued and turned over to environmental authorities…

blocks.text: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – A juvenile South Philippine Hawk-Eagle (Nisaetus pinskeri), an endangered raptor endemic to the country, was rescued and turned over to environmental authorities Sunday, September 6, offering a rare sign of hope for the survival of the threatened species.

The young bird was retrieved at Barangay Sas in Gutalac town, Zamboanga del Norte by a team from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Community Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO) Liloy.

Initial physical assessments revealed the eaglet is in good condition despite months away from its natural habitat. The juvenile raptor is currently housed at the CENRO Liloy Wildlife Holding Facility, where wildlife officers are conducting further evaluation and health monitoring to prepare the bird for eventual release back into the wild.

The bird’s journey to safety began three months ago when Justine Jay Sapalleda and his friends heard distress calls coming from a fallen nest in a nearby tree. Finding the crying eaglet vulnerable and abandoned, the children brought it home to protect it.

For three months, the Sapalleda family sheltered and fed the juvenile eagle a diet of fish and chicken meat. Unaware that keeping protected wildlife is illegal under Philippine law, the family raised the bird through its most delicate developmental stage before local resident Jessica Pagente learned of the situation and alerted CENRO Liloy.

“The timely report and the care extended by the Sapalleda family helped ensure the juvenile eagle’s safety and provided it with an opportunity to return to the wild,” CENRO Liloy chief Maribel Acama said, highlighting the vital role local communities play in conservation efforts.
Also known as Pinsker’s hawk-eagle, the species is classified as “endangered” under DENR Administrative Order No. 2019-09 due to severe habitat loss and poaching.

Following the turnover, CENRO Liloy reminded the public that holding or keeping wildlife is prohibited, urging citizens to immediately report displaced, injured, or threatened animals to the nearest DENR office for proper rescue and rehabilitation. INQ

articles.title: Army’s 4ID unveils Camp Evangelista museum in CDO
articles.summary: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — The storied legacy of the Army’s 4th Infantry Division (4ID) found a refreshed home on Monday, September 7, with the formal unveiling of the newly renovated Borromeo Hall at…

blocks.text: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — The storied legacy of the Army’s 4th Infantry Division (4ID) found a refreshed home on Monday, September 7, with the formal unveiling of the newly renovated Borromeo Hall at Camp Evangelista here.

Transformed into the official 4ID Museum, the upgraded facility now features an audio-visual room and a mini library built to safeguard and showcase the division’s decades of military heritage, traditions, and combat history.

The full overhaul was made possible through the sponsorship of Jose Vicente “Lito” Cabrera Sr. and his family — wife Denvi Tiu Cabrera, son Jose Vicente “JV” Jr., and daughter Michelle Cabrera Francisco.

The project was executed through 4ID’s Civil-Military Operations office (G7), with key support from the logistics office (G4), the 4th Installation Management Battalion, the Post Engineer Detachment, OLB Architectural Services, and the museum’s curatorial and historical team.
“This initiative would not have been made possible without the generosity and support of Mr. Cabrera,” said Maj. Gen. Marion Angcao, 4ID commander, during the ceremony.
“Sir, your contribution has helped us create a place where the history and legacy of those who served can be remembered and appreciated,” he added.

articles.title: Second-hand smoke causes to nearly 1.7M deaths globally – study
articles.summary: PARIS — More than 2.7 billion people including children have been exposed to second-hand smoke globally, contributing to nearly 1.7 million deaths in 2023, according to study published Tuesday…

blocks.text: PARIS — More than 2.7 billion people including children have been exposed to second-hand smoke globally, contributing to nearly 1.7 million deaths in 2023, according to study published Tuesday in The Lancet.

Tobacco remains a leading cause of disease globally, the study said, noting many “non-smokers exposed to second-hand smoke” were among the estimate total of 8 million people who died in 2023 of smoking-related illnesses.
“Exposure to second-hand smoke is a globally recognized health risk, with no safe level of inhalation,” it said.

By reviewing studies published in the US National Institutes of Health database PubMed along with population surveys, Tuesday’s study sought to estimate the prevalence of exposure to second-hand smoke and quantify the burden of disease in 204 countries and territories between 1990 and 2023.
Among the approximately 2.7 billion people exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023 were 767 million children aged 0 to 14, the study found.

This exposure is estimated to have resulted in 1.66 million premature deaths and causing premature disability and illness, leading with ischemic heart disease, a heart condition caused by insufficient oxygen supply to the heart muscle.
In children, exposure to second-hand smoke is estimated to have caused 5.2 million respiratory tract infections in 2023, it said.
People in proximity to someone lighting up are exposed to both the “sidestream smoke” from the burning tobacco product and smoke exhaled by the active smoker, the study explained.

“The sidestream component, which dominates the air non-smokers breathe, is unfiltered… carrying higher per-unit concentrations of the toxic and carcinogenic compounds” than that being inhaled by the active smoker, it said.

Despite significant declines in smoking prevalence globally since 1990, the absolute number of people exposed has remained stable due to population growth and increased exposure in Africa and the Middle East.
Women are also disproportionately affected by second-hand smoke, particularly in regions where smoking prevalence among women is low, it noted.
“Despite this substantial burden, (second-hand smoke) exposure remains rarely acknowledged as a major risk factor for female health,” it said.
The study called for governments to implement stronger tobacco controls in public places and in homes in order to better protect women and children from second-hand smoke. /dl

articles.title: Eiffel Tower shut by staff protest after women moved for religious visit
articles.summary: The mayor of Paris said an investigation would be launched into the incident, which left female employees "humiliated", according to a union representative.

blocks.text: The Eiffel Tower was closed on Monday after staff went on strike over female workers being removed for the visit of a Hindu religious group, workers and management said.
A delegation of around 100 people linked to the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) group visited the landmark in the French capital on Saturday.
Staff union representative Diane Davoine says as they arrived at the monument, women were told to move.

"During the visit of this delegation, women were asked to leave their places of work in order to place men there," she told Reuters. Davoine also said management had since apologised to workers over the incident.
"So that absolutely does not go down well with the employees, with women obviously, who are all humiliated by what happened, by the way some were treated," Davoine said.

She added: "Tensions mounted over the weekend, so this morning, the employees decided to meet: first, to open a dialogue with management, and second, to ensure that women are never treated this way at the company again."

Société d'Exploitation de la tour Eiffel (SETE), the company that operates the monument in Paris, confirmed the delegation had asked the visit be organised to limit "interactions with women", according to the AFP news agency.
The firm told AFP that "these conditions should not have been accepted".
They added they "were not in line with SETE's values, nor with the principles of equality between men and women".
SETE president Ariel Weil said: "It is clearly not an acceptable practice.
"I restate the Eiffel Tower's commitment to republican values and to the equality of men and women."
The BBC has contacted the Union Confédération générale du travail (CGT) for a response.
BAPS consecrated its first major temple in France on Sunday, in the suburbs of Paris.

In a statement on X, the BAPS temple in Paris said their trip was "arranged in conjunction with the Eiffel Tower team at the start of normal opening hours to avoid disrupting or inconveniencing others".
It apologised "for any pain or inconvenience caused", adding "we believe in the universal values of mutual respect and service".
On its website, BAPS describes itself as a "spiritual, volunteer-driven fellowship dedicated to improving society" through Hindu values.
It has temples in major cities around the world, including London, Los Angeles and Sydney.
Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire said there would be an investigation into the circumstances of the visit.
"I am taking note of the anger expressed by the employees of the Eiffel Tower, and I want to tell them that their discontent is legitimate," he wrote on X.
"Equality between women and men will never stop at the foot of our historical monuments, nor anywhere in this city. It must be applied everywhere, for everyone."
French hard-right leader Marine Le Pen said: "In France, we will never accept that the presence of women be 'limited'."

Former centre-right French Prime Minister Gabriel Attal, who has said he will run for the presidency next year, said: "In France, no culture, no belief, no worship, nothing nor anyone can come to dictate to women their place."
Yaël Braun-Pivet, the president of France's National Assembly, said: "I refuse to allow women to be compelled to step aside in order to meet the demands of foreign visitors."

articles.title: Highlights: Day 22 of Sara Duterte impeachment trial | Sept. 7, 2026
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – The 22nd day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial focused on the identities of alleged recipients of confidential funds released by the Office of the Vice…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The 22nd day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial focused on the identities of alleged recipients of confidential funds released by the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd).

Philippine Statistics Authority Assistant National Statistician Marizza Grande testified for the prosecution and confirmed that several names listed as confidential fund payees could not be found in the agency’s civil registry records.

Grande’s testimony covered the unusual or unique names of individuals who signed acknowledgment receipts used by the Office of the Vice President and the Department of Education to liquidate their P612.5 million in confidential funds.

In a notable development, defense counsel Justin Gular, responding to a query from Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros, acknowledged for the first time during the proceedings that the names on the acknowledgment receipts are aliases.
Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo said the use of aliases could be forgivable, but described the similar signatures and handwriting on the receipts as very questionable.

Presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero separately announced that the impeachment court may summon witnesses on its own should it see the need to, after Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo expressed hope that former VPSPG officials Col. Dennis Nolasco and Col. Raymund Lachica would be called despite the prosecution indicating it no longer needed them.

Meanwhile, Senator Robin Padilla, a self-described ally of the Duterte family, argued in a manifestation that the immunity from suit enjoyed by the president should be extended to the vice president, citing the constitutional purpose of protecting impeachable officers from harassment and distraction.
Outside the impeachment court, Malacañang assured Sara Duterte the PNP would not be used as a weapon against her, after she posted bail Saturday on three grave threats counts./dp
